title: Live server never initializes the books table (schema created on a discarded connection)
evidence: src/main.rs:79 serves `rusqlite::Connection::open_in_memory()` with no DDL applied; src/main.rs:80 `models::create_connection("in-memory").ok()` creates the `books` table on a SEPARATE on-disk file connection (literal file named 'in-memory') that is immediately dropped. Confirmed by the stray on-disk SQLite file `in-memory` in the workspace whose `.tables` shows `books` and `.schema` matches models::TABLE_DEF. Every DB-touching route (POST/GET/PUT/DELETE /books) fails at runtime with 'no such table: books'. Tests pass (test_coverage=1.0) only because tests build their own schema-initialized connection via create_db()/get_test_conn() (main.rs:107-111, database.rs:144-148). This is the exact regression FEEDBACK.md said to fix; it was NOT fixed.
suggestion: In main(), apply the schema to the served connection: `db.execute_batch(models::TABLE_DEF).unwrap();` after opening it (or replace lines 79-80 with `let db = models::create_connection("books.db").unwrap();`). Remove the discarded `create_connection("in-memory").ok()` call.

The verify-on-stop step did not catch the persisting live-server defect.

title: README claims in-memory SQLite storage that does not actually work on the live server
evidence: README.md:20 states 'Storage: In-memory SQLite database', but the served in-memory connection has no `books` table, so the documented runtime behavior is broken (see R7).
suggestion: Fix the R7 wiring bug so the documented storage actually functions; consider file-backed persistence to match the discarded create_connection() intent.
